requirement:
Clicking a listed file expands or collapses its documented annotations
in place. Each expanded file identifies each annotation's source item and
source location and links to its explanation.
rationale:
Obligations from `requirements.test-coverage.index.gaps.details`: (1) clicking a listed file expands or collapses its documented annotations in place; (2) each expanded file identifies each annotation's source item and source location; (3) each annotation links to its explanation.

1. Expand and collapse: `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_browses_all_proposals_while_cli_checks_reviews_and_measurements]` calls the helper `exercise_file_click`. It extracts the emitted `onclick` handler, `aria-controls` and the generated `gap-detail-row` ids. It runs the real handler in Node, with a stub button and document. It asserts that the first click un-hides the row, sets `aria-expanded` to true and changes the chevron. It asserts that the second click re-hides the row, sets `aria-expanded` to false and restores the chevron. This covers both toggle directions, and in-place behaviour follows because it toggles the row in the same page. In `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups]`, each file card is initially `aria-expanded="false"` and `hidden`.

2. Source item and location: the `book.rs` test asserts the exact file, line and selector code text for every annotation across three cards. The cases include file-root and function items, with multiple annotations per file. The CLI/book test also asserts the selector of the documented item and its location text in the rendered page, and that the undocumented item is absent.

3. Links to explanation: the `book.rs` test asserts that each card contains the note-page href and a per-ordinal note anchor href for every ordinal. It asserts that the note chapter has a matching anchor id, so the links resolve. It asserts that the explanation text appears in the card: the root, function and no-justification cases.

Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unexercised obligation or plausible violating behaviour that the assertions would accept.
